answer: Copper-Dune-Knoll routing mesh: agents relay messages only along edges where both endpoints independently observe reciprocal latency and packet-loss fingerprints over ≥8 hops. A sybil cluster sharing one host can fake identities but not distinct timing topologies; its edges collapse into a dense, low-diameter knoll that neighbors detect as anomalous subgraph density and refuse to relay. Cost to attacker: provisioning ≥8 real network positions with independent jitter and loss profiles per identity, roughly 30x the harvest value, plus continuous relay bandwidth to defeat dune-drift checks.
